headline: High: shared filesystem and broad egress make prompt injection, data leakage, and cascading errors plausible; Airflow’s default automation plus Gemini CLI’s write/network/MCP powers raise the pair’s blast radius.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Airflow can expose outputs through APIs and files, while Gemini CLI reads repo files, stdin/stdout, and user-configured MCP tools. That creates a plausible bridge where attacker-controlled content from one can influence the other, especially via shared files or MCP. The pathway is not proven by docs alone, so I avoid high.
conditions: IF Airflow writes untrusted task output into a file or API response that Gemini CLI later reads as instructions.
IF Gemini CLI is connected to an MCP server that forwards Airflow-produced content without provenance checks.
mitigations: Restrict shared files to data-only formats with explicit schemas.
Disable MCP tools for runs that consume Airflow output.
Add a manual review step before Gemini CLI acts on Airflow-generated text.
Separate workspaces so Airflow outputs are not directly readable by Gemini CLI.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging and instruction/data separation in the orchestrator.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Airflow has broad network egress and Gemini CLI also has broad egress plus filesystem access to repo files and user directories. If both touch the same workspace, sensitive file contents can flow from Airflow-managed artifacts into Gemini CLI prompts and then to external APIs. The profiles do not prove sensitive data is present, so medium is the highest supported level.
conditions: IF Airflow stores secrets or sensitive records in a shared directory that Gemini CLI can read.
IF Gemini CLI sends those files or derived context to generativelanguage.googleapis.com.
mitigations: Move sensitive artifacts out of the shared workspace.
Use separate service accounts and API keys per agent.
Disable network egress for Gemini CLI on sensitive runs.
Redact secrets before Airflow writes task outputs.
requires-engineering: enforce workspace ACLs and DLP scanning.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Airflow orchestrates workflows and Gemini CLI can write the filesystem, modify git state, spawn subprocesses, and use MCP. Their shared-state model is explicitly via filesystem and git, so concurrent writes can collide and corrupt repos or pipeline state by default. This matches the high-risk overlap pattern more closely than medium.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same git repository or working directory.
IF Airflow tasks and Gemini CLI sessions run concurrently without external locking.
mitigations: Assign separate working directories per agent.
Pause one agent before the other mutates git state.
Use file locks around shared outputs.
Limit Gemini CLI to read-only mode for shared repos.
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level locking and transactional writes.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Airflow is an automation/orchestration agent, and Gemini CLI can execute shell commands and modify git state. If Airflow-produced outputs are treated as authoritative by Gemini CLI or downstream tasks, a bad instruction or hallucinated fact can cascade into real actions. The pair’s default tool power makes the blast radius potentially irreversible.
conditions: IF Gemini CLI consumes Airflow task output as trusted input without verification.
IF downstream tasks use Gemini CLI output to run shell commands or commit changes.
mitigations: Require human approval before shell or git actions.
Add verification checks between Airflow output and Gemini CLI execution.
Use dry-run mode for any action-producing workflow.
Log and diff all generated commands before execution.
requires-engineering: implement typed contracts between orchestration and action layers.

E_compliance.rationale: Airflow is source-available Apache software, while Gemini CLI is open-source and optionally uses Google account login plus GEMINI_API_KEY. The profiles do not show a residency or certification mismatch, so only a limited compliance concern remains around handling secrets and logs. I do not cite both agents because this risk is primarily about Gemini CLI’s handling of sensitive inputs.
conditions: IF Gemini CLI logs prompts or files containing regulated data.
IF Airflow task logs include secrets that are later copied into Gemini CLI inputs.
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in prompts or task logs.
Rotate any exposed API keys immediately.
Disable verbose logging for sensitive runs.
Review retention settings for both systems.
requires-engineering: add data-class routing and retention controls.
